name: Zig
hypothesis: Explicit allocation, C interop, specialization and SIMD

name: Odin
hypothesis: Data-layout-oriented native implementation and explicit allocator control

name: Nim
hypothesis: Metaprogrammed native code and interop may reduce implementation burden
disqualifying_questions: memory model, exceptions, concurrency and distribution

name: Julia
hypothesis: Numerical ecosystem and specialized kernels may reduce time to a correct implementation
disqualifying_questions: compilation/startup, allocation, type stability and service boundary

name: Pony
hypothesis: Reference-capability actor model offers a distinct concurrency design
required_baseline: Current Rust/Go actor or async scheduler
disqualifying_questions: runtime integration, cancellation, tail latency and deploy support

name: Mojo
hypothesis: Specialized numerical implementation with native/GPU facilities
disqualifying_questions: toolchain availability, target backend, ABI and distribution

name: CUDA + CUTLASS/CuTe
hypothesis: Direct kernel/library control and specialized library primitives
disqualifying_questions: architecture restrictions, memory traffic, launch and transfer cost

name: Triton
required_baseline: Framework compiled kernels and CUDA baseline
disqualifying_questions: shape/dtype coverage, compile cost and resource occupancy

name: Trident (kakaobrain)
hypothesis: Triton-based kernel ideas might be reusable
disqualifying_questions: archived since 2023; resolve intended identity; no automatic production adoption

name: ISPC
disqualifying_questions: vector width, tail handling and host-call cost

name: TileLang
hypothesis: Alternative kernel abstraction and optimization space

name: Futhark
hypothesis: Array compiler may generate competitive parallel code
disqualifying_questions: supported operations, backend and host interface

name: Halide
hypothesis: Algorithm and scheduling separation gives another optimization axis
disqualifying_questions: scheduling effort, target, memory and whole-pipeline timing
